state.proposal: Review a proposed error notation family in Can: error missing{str key} declares fields, emits {missing} names possible domain failures, and missing{key} builds an error with positional arguments. No braces are proposed for statement blocks, record construction, function calls, match arms, relay call, or standard failures; arrays still use []. The task is to judge the design, not implement it.
state.language_facts: Can now treats bare { and } as invalid punctuation, using indentation for blocks, () for calls plus records/errors, and [] for arrays plus emits bounds. Existing equivalents are error missing(str key), emits [missing], and missing(key). The bound is mandatory even when empty, as emits []; in a callable array, emits [][] could instead read emits {}[]. Generic error data can nest as all_failed<T>([missing(key)]). Declared error fields and constructed values are positional.
state.meaning: Nominal error instances are ordinary immutable data until a terminal completion emits one; ok results, sum variants, assertions, and fixture inputs may contain them without failing. A bare forwarding arm retains the prior occurrence, whereas reconstructing an error is not forwarding that occurrence. Standard failures have a separate channel, are excluded from emits, and are not constructible by an application. The proposed punctuation must preserve these contracts exactly.
state.constraints: There is no backward-compatibility need for external users. Can source is heavily authored by coding agents, so consistent and unambiguous notation is valuable. A full syntax migration would touch compiler front end, formatter, editor integration, and examples. No controlled source-reading or authoring trial has demonstrated a benefit.

direction.instructions: Recommend one provisional grammar direction from the listed alternatives, considering whether the three brace roles form a helpful visual family and whether their positional contents will be understood correctly.

criteria.full_triad: Mark typed error declarations, finite emits sets, and all error-value constructors with braces, while preserving the present rules for non-error code, matching, propagation, and standard faults.
criteria.bound_and_constructor: Mark error sets and error-value creation with braces but leave the field list in error declarations parenthesized; retain the current semantics and other syntax.
criteria.declaration_and_constructor: Use matching braced shapes for declaring an error and building its positional value, while the allowed-error set continues to be written emits [E].
criteria.bound_only: Reserve curly braces just for finite emits membership; keep the declaration field list and error constructor arguments in parentheses.
criteria.retain_current: Continue with the brace-free source grammar: error declarations and construction use (), and emits bounds use [].
